column1: # A chapter's art, and where it came from.
# One row per chapter. `make_chapter_art.py` reads the chapter's own JSON for the
# names — its `mapStrips`, its backdrop and every backdrop a level overrides — and
# for the palette each backdrop is graded to. This file only says which source
# images those names are cut from, because that is the one thing the content
# cannot state: a chapter names art, it does not name the pack it was cut from.
# Re-running is safe and is the point. A retune of a level's `accent`/`slate`
# regrades its backdrop with no second place to edit, which is why the palette
# lives in the chapter file and not here.
# columns
#   chapter    the chapter id, matching Content/chapters/<id>.json
#   map        one tall image, sliced bottom-upward into `mapStrips`, or `-` when this
#              chapter's strips are not cut by this tool
#   backdrops  comma-separated sources for the board backdrops, or `-` when this chapter's
#              backdrop is not this row's to cut. Windows are taken
#              across them in turn, so two wide images comfortably feed ten glades.
#              A source may be a `+`-joined **stack** of layer files, composited bottom
#              upward — which is what a layered pack is for. Three of these were overlay
#              layers named on their own (71% and 75% transparent) and were being
#              flattened onto undefined paper; `opened` now refuses a stack whose bottom
#              layer is not opaque, because that failure is invisible in every other gate.
# Sources are outside the repo (they are licensed packs, not project files). Pass
# the folder they were extracted into with --source; paths below are relative to it.
# chapter
# c01_shallows, and the three chapters that borrow its backdrops (f01_lightfall draws
# play_2, k01_grovekeeper play_4, b01_thicket play_6), had no row here at all — so nine
# of the game's forty-one board backdrops were the one part of the art pipeline nothing
# could re-cut. Those four share a hand-made strip set, hence the `-`.
# Two cloud layers rather than two paintings: the Shallows is the first chapter anybody
# meets and its nine backdrops sit behind five different boards (f01, k01 and b01 all
# borrow one), so what they owe is a friendly sky and no scene of their own to argue
# with. The layer art also carries none of the dummy lettering the preview sheets in
# these packs do.
c01_shallows
c02_millvale
c03_amberwood

column1: c04_nightbriar
# `Backgrounds/1.png` is the pack's placeholder sheet — two blocks of dummy lettering on
# a flat panel — and it was what the Hollow's only backdrop was cut from: blurred and
# graded, the words survived as two legible smudges. It reached no player only because
# h01_emberfall is not in the manifest; nothing in this repository could have caught it,
# which is why a source is looked at before it is named.
h01_emberfall
# f02_glasswater is the first non-glade chapter to get a map of its own, and it needed one:
# it drew `strip0..5` — c01_shallows' hand-made set — so Lightfall's two chapters were the same
# painting, which is what the glade chapters never do.
# There are four tall map paintings in these packs and all four were already cut, so this is the
# case the fourth column exists for: the source is c03_amberwood's, the output files and
# addresses are f02's own, and `night` at 0.60 pulls it to Glasswater's cold slate so the two
# chapters read as two places rather than one picture twice. The alternatives were looked at and
# rejected — the island map is the one f01 already draws, the dark map is a Halloween scene
# (pumpkins and a gravestone), and the top-down map crops to 59% of its width at six strips.
# The backdrop is `-`. Every non-glade chapter borrows one of c01_shallows' nine (f01 draws
# play_2, k01 play_4, b01 play_6, f02 play_8), and a row naming a source for one would re-cut a
# picture four chapters share, graded to whichever chapter the tool was last run for.
f02_glasswater
x02_lab
